rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recounts every deed with full knowledge and was never absent from any outward or inward act; this exposure intensifies the rebuke after people admit wrongdoing and witnesses testify.
rows.anchor: بل علمنا محيط بجميع أعمالهم، ظاهرها وباطنها

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: A person is reminded of each deed and saying in worldly life until the interrogation reaches the last thing he did and said.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: يقال للرجل منهم أتذكر يوم فعلت كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about recounting with knowledge establishes knowledge as an attribute of God and refutes those who deny that God knows.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله بعلم دليل على إثبات هذه الصفة لله تعالى وإبطال لقول من قال لا علم لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes disagree whether the weighing is a real balance or a figure for complete justice, sound judgment, and exact reckoning.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا هل ثم وزن وميزان حقيقة أم ذلك عبارة عن إظهار العدل التام

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila, preceded in this view by Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Aʿmash, deny a literal balance and take heaviness and lightness as abundance or scarcity of good deeds.
rows.anchor: فذهبت المعتزلة إلى إنكار الميزان وتقدمهم إلى هذا مجاهد والضحاك والأعمش

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: The majority affirm a real balance with a shaft, two pans, and a tongue, shown to all creatures to establish proof, justice, and the end of excuses.
rows.anchor: وقال جمهور الأمة بالأول وأن الميزان له عمود وكفتان ولسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible balance confirms the judgment alongside questioning, people’s admissions, testimony by limbs, prophets, angels, and witnesses.
rows.anchor: تأكيدا للحجة وإظهارا للنصفة وقطعا للمعذرة كما يسألهم عن أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say the weighed objects are the records on which deeds were written; God creates heaviness or lightness in them, while reports about the balance’s dimensions and form have unsound chains.
rows.anchor: أن الموزون هي الصحائف التي أثبتت فيها الأعمال، فيحدث الله تعالى فيها ثقلا وخفة

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: The majority explain plural balances by the multiplicity of objects weighed, although there is one balance.
rows.anchor: وجمعت الموازين باعتبار الموزونات والميزان واحد، هذا قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan holds that every person has a separate balance on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: لكل أحد يوم القيامة ميزان على حدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balances can also stand for good deeds by ellipsis: the balance-pan of a person’s weighed deeds becomes heavy or light.
rows.anchor: وقد يعبر عن الحسنات بالموازين فيكون ذلك على حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, weighing is the subject and the time expression supplies its predicate, with the sense that the weighing occurs when God questions people and recounts their deeds on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ وخبره ظرف الزمان والتقدير والوزن كائن يوم أن نسألهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word true may qualify the weighing, or the time phrase may modify weighing and true may be its predicate.
rows.anchor: والحق صفة للوزن ويجوز أن يكون يومئذ ظرفا للوزن معمولا له والحق خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase about God’s signs attaches to wronging because the verb includes the sense of denying or rejecting, and rejection takes bi-.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا التقسيم هو بالنسبة للمؤمنين من أطاع ومن عصى وللكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent division includes obedient and sinful believers as well as unbelievers, so unbelievers’ deeds are weighed.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا التقسيم هو بالنسبة للمؤمنين من أطاع ومن عصى وللكفار فتوزن أعمال الكفار

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others say unbelievers receive no balance and are not judged, citing the verse that their deeds become scattered dust; on this view only believers’ deeds are weighed.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: لا ينصب لهم ميزان ولا يحاسبون لقوله وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording recalls the earlier expression in al-Anʿam; the address returns to those commanded to follow revelation, with the intervening history serving as admonition about worldly outcomes and the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: تقدم معنى مكناكم في قوله في أول الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural maʿāyish has two possible patterns in the singular, with the vowel on the ʿayn either i or u, according to Sibawayh.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون وزنها مفعلة ومفعلة بكسر العين وضمها قالهما سيبويه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ gives the singular maʿīsha with fatḥa on its ʿayn.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: معيشة بفتح عين الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿāyish means food, drink, and other necessities of living; the word began as a verbal noun and came to denote the means by which one lives.
rows.anchor: وهي في الأصل مصدر تنزل منزلة الآلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis supplies a deleted word: the verse means means of livelihood such as farming, harvesting, and trade, which lead to what sustains life.
rows.anchor: وقيل على حذف مضاف التقدير أسباب معايش كالزرع والحصد والتجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation takes livelihoods as kinds of benefit, whether God produces them directly, such as fruit, or people acquire them; both call for gratitude.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعائش وجوه المنافع وهي إما يحدثه الله ابتداء كالثمار

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read maʿāyish without hamza because the singular’s yāʾ is original; only an added yāʾ, as in ṣaḥāʾif, is hamzated in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: معايش بالياء وهو القياس لأن الياء في المفرد هي أصل لا زائدة

rows.speaker: الأعرج وزيد بن علي والأعمش وخارجة عن نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: These readers transmit maʿāʾish with hamza; although irregular by analogy, Abu Hayyan says their reliable transmission must be accepted.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج وزيد بن علي والأعمش وخارجة عن نافع وابن عامر في رواية: معائش بالهمزة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the Basran grammarians regard hamzating maʿāyish as an error, with no basis beyond analogy to ṣaḥīfa and ṣaḥāʾif, and says the reading should not be relied on.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: جميع نحاة البصرة تزعم أن همزها خطأ

rows.speaker: المازني
rows.claim: Al-Mazini claims the reading originated with Nafiʿ, who did not know Arabic; Abu Hayyan rejects this as false, noting other transmitters and that eloquence does not require grammatical scholarship.
rows.anchor: وقال المازني: أصل أخذ هذه القراءة عن نافع ولم يكن يدري ما العربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the Basran dismissal: multiple eloquent, reliable readers independently transmit the hamzated form, so their Qurʾanic reading is accepted despite grammarians’ objections.
rows.anchor: فوجب قبول ما نقلوه إلينا ولا مبالاة بمخالفة نحاة البصرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ reports that Arabs sometimes hamzate words like this by imagining them to follow the faʿīla pattern and analogizing mafʿala to it.
rows.anchor: ربما همزت العرب هذا وشبهه يتوهمون أنها فعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax of little do you give thanks parallels the syntax of little do you remember in the earlier verse.
rows.anchor: وإعراب قليلا ما تشكرون كإعراب قليلا ما تذكرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After distinguishing the obedient from the disobedient, the passage recalls the first such test: angels obeyed God’s command to prostrate to Adam while Iblis refused.
rows.anchor: أخذ ينبه على أن هذا التقسيم كان في البدء الأول من أمر الله للملائكة بالسجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation from nonexistence and formation in this remarkable shape display the Creator’s artistry; the address apparently includes all Adam’s descendants.
rows.anchor: إبراز الشيء من العدم الصرف إلى الوجود والتصوير في هذه الصورة الغريبة الشكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the address is to all humanity, thumma may mean and rather than chronological sequence, or may sequence the narration rather than events; the latter is the easier reading.
rows.anchor: إما أن تكون فيه ثم بمعنى الواو فلم ترتب ويكون الترتيب بين الخلق والتصوير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take thumma chronologically and differ over the addressee: Adam alone, all descendants, Adam in the first clauses and descendants in the second, or Adam as an honorific plural.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في المخاطب، فقيل المراد به آدم وهو من إطلاق الجمع على الواحد

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The report attributed through al-ʿAwfi says the first two clauses address Adam and the later command is narrated in sequence rather than time.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا العوفي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report says Adam was created and formed in Paradise, then his descendants were formed in his loins at the covenant, so the sequence is chronological.
rows.anchor: خلقناكم لآدم ثم صورناكم لبنيه يعني في صلبه عند أخذ الميثاق

rows.speaker: الحارث عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: This account places humanity’s creation in Adam’s back and its formation in the wombs.
rows.anchor: فروى الحارث عن ابن عباس خلقناكم في ظهر آدم ثم صورناكم في الأرحام

rows.speaker: ابن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: This report says people were created in men’s loins and formed in women’s wombs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير عنه خلقناكم في أصلاب الرجل ثم صورناكم في أرحام النساء

rows.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة والضحاك والأعمش
rows.claim: These authorities also explain creation in men’s loins and formation in women’s wombs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير عنه خلقناكم في أصلاب الرجل ثم صورناكم في أرحام النساء

rows.speaker: ابن السائب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib says people were created as drops in men’s loins and women’s chests, then formed when the drops joined in the wombs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السائب خلقناكم نطفا في أصلاب الرجال وترائب النساء

rows.speaker: معمر بن راشد
rows.claim: Maʿmar transmits from an unnamed scholar that people were created in their mothers’ wombs and then given hearing and sight there.
rows.anchor: وقال معمر بن راشد حاكيا عن بعض أهل العلم خلقناكم في بطون أمهاتكم

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: A view cited from al-Qadi Abu Yaʿla supplies a deleted noun: God created people’s spirits, then formed their bodies.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخطاب لبني آدم إلا أنه على حذف مضاف التقدير ولقد خلقنا أرواحكم ثم صورنا أجسامكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view supplies your father Adam and takes thumma in its ordinary chronological sense, with an interval between events.
rows.anchor: وقيل التقدير ولقد خلقنا أباكم ثم صورنا أباكم ثم قلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the turning-of-address explanation, present descendants are addressed while Adam is intended, as elsewhere Israelites are addressed about their ancestors.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من تلوين الخطاب يخاطب العين ويراد به الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tribal poem addresses descendants about their ancestors’ battle at Dhi Qar, illustrating speech directed to one generation while referring to another.
rows.anchor: وهذه الوقعة كانت لآبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause saying Iblis was not among those who prostrated has no syntactic position and reinforces the exclusion’s denial, as the next verse’s he refused and was arrogant does.
rows.anchor: جملة لا موضع لها من الإعراب مؤكدة لمعنى ما أخرجه الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading treats la as emphatic and redundant: the question asks what prevented Iblis from fulfilling prostration, matching the parallel wording without la.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن لا زائدة تفيد التوكيد والتحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic examples are offered for redundant la, but Abu Hayyan rejects the first as proof because la may be a conjunction with an omitted complement.
rows.anchor: وأقول لا حجة في البيت الأول إذ يحتمل أن لا تكون فيه لا زائدة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj construes la as the object and al-bukhl as its substitute in the second poetic example.
rows.anchor: فقال الزجاج لا مفعولة والبخل بدل منها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reports a different vocalization: la is genitive through annexation to al-bukhl, since la can be spoken without denoting miserliness.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: الرواية فيه لا البخل بخفض اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan offers another parsing of the second poem: al-bukhl is a purpose object and la is the direct object.
rows.anchor: وهو أن ينتصب البخل على أنه مفعول من أجله ولا مفعولة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others deny that la is redundant, either supplying a missing phrase that makes sense of the negation or taking mana as meaning forbade or told you not to prostrate.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: لا في أن لا تسجد ليست زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s answer does not directly answer the question, but implies that he considered his superior origin a reason to refuse serving Adam.
rows.anchor: هذا ليس بجواب مطابق للسؤال لكنه يتضمن الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s argument assumes fire is superior because it is bright, celestial, subtle, light, hot, and active, whereas clay is dark, dense, heavy, cold, and receptive.
rows.anchor: النار جسم مشرق علوي لطيف خفيف حار يابس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those defending Iblis’s comparison say an origin made from the better substance should be better and should not serve an inferior, as reason would reject eminent scholars serving lesser ones.
rows.anchor: فالمخلوق من الأفضل أفضل فلا يؤمر الأفضل بخدمة المفضول

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal argues that clay’s gravity, patience, humility, and forbearance suit Adam’s repentance and forgiveness, while fire’s volatility and elevation suit Iblis’s pride, curse, and punishment.
rows.anchor: قاله القفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two materials are equally created inanimate matter, so the claimed premise that every fire-origin is superior to every clay-origin fails.
rows.anchor: وهما في درجة واحدة من حيث هما جماد مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Material origin does not establish the superiority of a creature’s form, since excellence is God’s gift; a believing Abyssinian is better than a Qurashi unbeliever.
rows.anchor: لا يدل من كانت مادته أفضل على أنه تكون صورته أفضل إذا الفضيلة عطية من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Hasan, and Ibn Sirin call Iblis the first to reason by analogy; Ibn Abbas says he erred and that religious opinion-based analogy associates its user with Iblis.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن وابن سيرين أول من قاس إبليس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: They say worship of the sun and moon arose through analogical reasoning.
rows.anchor: وقالا: وما عبدت الشمس والقمر إلا بالمقاييس

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars say Iblis’s analogy failed because he did not know that the spirit breathed into Adam was not made of clay.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: أخطأ قياسه وذهب علمه أن الروح الذي نفخ في آدم ليس من طين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story does not disprove analogy generally: Iblis used it where an explicit text applied, making this instance invalid, unlike cases without a text.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة فيها لأنه قياس في مورد النص فهو فاسد فلا يدل على بطلان القياس حيث لا نص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke over disobeying God’s command indicates that an unqualified command entails obligation and immediate performance; otherwise Iblis would not merit blame then or later.
rows.anchor: على أن مطلق الأمر يدل على الوجوب ويدل على الفور لذم إبليس على امتناعه من السجود في الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Iblis refused prostration out of imagined superiority over Adam, God answers with a descent from high to low.
rows.anchor: لما كان امتناعه من السجود لسبب ظهور شفوقه على آدم عند نفسه قابله الله بالهبوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in descend from it has no expressed antecedent, and most interpretations identify the place or status in different ways.
rows.anchor: والضمير في منها لم يتقدم له مفسر يعود عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they were in the Garden of Eden, not the Garden of Eternity, and Adam was created in Eden.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كانوا في جنة عدن لا في جنة الخلد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says Iblis was first expelled from Paradise to heaven, where he tempted Adam and Eve from outside, then later ordered down from heaven with them and the serpent.
rows.anchor: أهبط أولا وأخرج من الجنة وصار في السماء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes it as descent from heaven, abode of obedient, humble angels, to earth, home of disobedient and arrogant beings.
rows.anchor: فاهبط منها من السماء التي هي مكان المطيعين المتواضعين

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abu Rawq says Iblis was ordered down from his former shape after its brightness was darkened and altered.
rows.anchor: يعود على صورته التي كان فيها لأنه افتخر أنه من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s request to live until resurrection acknowledges resurrection and implies Adam will have descendants who inhabit earth and die; he seeks time to tempt them.
rows.anchor: هذا يدل على إقراره بالبعث وعلمه بأن آدم سيكون له ذرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in they are raised refers to people supplied by the sense, since no antecedent occurs in the wording.
rows.anchor: فالضمير في يبعثون عائد على ما دل عليه المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allowing Iblis time tests people through the choice to obey or resist him, magnifying reward for resistance and sustaining punishment for compliance.
rows.anchor: حكمة استنظاره وإن كان ذلك سببا للغواية والفتنة إن في ذلك ابتلاء العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage does not state an endpoint for the reprieve, unlike the versions in al-Hijr and Sad that specify the known appointed time.
rows.anchor: ولم يأت هنا بغاية للانتظار وجاء مغيا في الحجر وفي ص بقوله إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reprieved group may mean people whose lives were unusually long but still ended at differing appointed times, not those living forever.
rows.anchor: من الطائفة التي تأخرت أعمارها كثيرا حتى جاءت آجالها على اختلاف أوقاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the reprieved as a large group, like the people of Jonah.
rows.anchor: وقيل من المنظرين جمع كثير مثل قوم يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in Iblis’s oath is for swearing and mā is a verbal noun; Abu Hayyan prefers Ibn ʿAtiyya’s causal or reciprocal sense as fitting the story better.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الباء للقسم وما مصدرية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Iblis swore by God’s leading him astray because this divine act was a good act that exposed him to eternal felicity.
rows.anchor: وإنما أقسم بالإغواء لأنه كان تكليفا من أحسن أفعال الله

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya treats the bāʾ as causal or recompensing, like saying that because someone honored you, you will honor him; Abu Hayyan says this better fits the account.
rows.anchor: وعبر ابن عطية عنها بأن يراد بها معنى المجازاة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the oath bāʾ cannot attach directly to the coming oath response because the oath lam blocks it, so it attaches to an omitted swear verb.
rows.anchor: تعلقت بفعل القسم المحذوف تقديره فبما أغويتني أقسم بالله لأقعدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan notes that the grammatical claim that the oath lam blocks the bāʾ from the response is disputed, not universally accepted.
rows.anchor: ليس حكما مجمعا عليه بل في ذلك خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A minority takes mā as an interrogative asking by what God caused the error, then begins the oath; this is weakened because the written alif is retained unusually.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما استفهامية كأنه استفهم عن السبب الذي أغواه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and most interpreters glossed aghwaytanī as You led me astray.
rows.anchor: معنى أغويتني أضللتني قاله ابن عباس والأكثرون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan glosses aghwaytanī as You cursed me.
rows.anchor: أو لعنتني قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari glosses aghwaytanī as You destroyed me.
rows.anchor: أو أهلكتني قاله ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpreter glosses the word as You disappointed me.
rows.anchor: أو خيبتني قاله بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other lexical explanations are that God cast Iblis into error, named him misguided because of his pride, placed him in error or punishment, decreed blameworthy acts, or introduced pride into him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ألقيتني غاويا، وقيل: سميتني غاويا لتكبري عن السجود

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets the phrase as God’s requiring an act that led Iblis into error, comparing the angels’ remaining steadfast though better in person and rank.
rows.anchor: وهو تكليفه إياه ما وقع به في الغي

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says God commanded prostration and Iblis’s pride drove him to disobey; he will strive to mislead humans as they caused his own ruin.
rows.anchor: وعن الأصم أمرتني بالسجود فحملني الأنف على معصيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says al-Zamakhshari and al-Asamm interpret the verse according to Muʿtazili doctrine, denying that God truly causes misguidance; the same evasion appears in the gloss found me misguided.
rows.anchor: وهو والأصم فسرا على مذهب الاعتزال في نفي نسبة الإغواء حقيقة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb rebukes the Qadariyya: Iblis knew more about God than they did because he acknowledged that God guides and misguides.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: قاتل الله القدرية لإبليس أعلم بالله منهم

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus told a jurist accused of Qadarism to leave or be removed, then said Iblis understood God better because he said God had led him astray while the jurist claimed to misguide himself.
rows.anchor: فقال له طاوس: تقوم أو تقام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari dismisses the Tawus anecdote as fabrications of the determinists and adds a disparaging comment about it.
rows.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري هذه الحكاية من تكاذيب المجبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qʿada means remaining fixed in a place; the accusative ṣirāṭ is best treated as a direct object by construing the verb as remain upon or adhere to.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالقعود عن الثبوت في المكان والثابت فيه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ṣirāṭ is accusative after deleting the preposition ʿalā, analogized to striking someone on the back or belly.
rows.anchor: وانتصب صراطك على إسقاط على قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says deleting a preposition this way is not productive by analogy; taking ṣirāṭ as a locative is also weak because a specific road requires a preposition.
rows.anchor: وإسقاط حرف الجر لا ينقاس في مثل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers construing sit as adhere so ṣirāṭ is its direct object; the straight path is Islam, which leads to Paradise.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يضمن لأقعدن معنى ما يتعدى بنفسه فينتصب الصراط على أنه مفعول به

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وعون بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿud and ʿAwn identifies the path as the Meccan road, especially the known Satan’s Pass where people are diverted from pilgrimage; Abu Hayyan considers this unlikely.
rows.anchor: ويضعف ما روي عن ابن مسعود وعون بن عبد الله أنه طريق مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s sitting across the path means intercepting people on Islam’s road as an enemy blocks travelers.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قعوده أنه يعترض لهم على طريق الإسلام

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says Satan intercepted Adam’s paths to Islam, migration, and jihad; the man resisted each argument and was promised Paradise.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث «إن الشيطان قعد لابن آدم بأطرقه نهاه عن الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming from four directions is an idiom for Satan’s determined whispering and misguidance from every possible side, not a literal four-direction arrival.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن إتيانه من هذه الجهات الأربع كناية عن وسوسته وإغوائه له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation says the front is doubt about the afterlife and resurrection, while the rear is temptation by worldly life; Ibn Abbas also transmits the reverse.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: من بين أيديهم الآخرة أشككهم فيها وأنه لا بعث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the right as truth and the left as falsehood; another report from him makes them good deeds and sins.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا وعن النخعي والحكم بن عتبة عكس هذا، وعنه وعن أيمانهم الحق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the first two directions are where people are supported and the latter two where they are not supported.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الأولان حيث ينصرون والآخران حيث لا ينصرون

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih takes the first two as truth and falsehood and the last two as the afterlife and this world.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح الأولان الحق والباطل والآخران الآخرة والدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations distribute Satan’s attacks across hope and forgetfulness of death, ease and hardship, past and remaining life, possessions and poverty, urging disobedience in each sphere.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأولان بفسحة الأمل وبنسيان الأجل والآخران فيما تيسر وفيما تعسر

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi transmits a philosophical interpretation: imagination, estimation, desire, and anger occupy four brain or heart locations and generate states that defeat spiritual happiness; external devils whisper through them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي حاكيا عن من سماه هو حكماء الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan considers the faculty theory remote from Arabic and religious usage; its adherents explain omission of above and below by saying no corrupting faculties reside there.
rows.anchor: وهو بعيد من مناحي كلام العرب والمتشرعين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says above was omitted because God’s mercy descends from above, and below because arrival from below would be disturbing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لم يقل من فوقهم لأن رحمة الله تنزل عليهم من فوقهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the varied prepositions with a linguistic analogy: sitting on someone’s right differs from sitting away from him, and directional prepositions vary as with shooting from, on, or off a bow.
rows.anchor: فلما سمعناهم يقولون: جلس عن يمينه وعلى يمينه وعن شماله وعلى شماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says front and rear take min because attack most commonly comes from them; front precedes rear as the bold direct assault precedes stealth from behind.
rows.anchor: إنما خص بين الأيدي والخلف بحرف الابتداء الذي هو أمكن في الإتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right and left take ʿan because the enemy less often approaches there; the right comes first because it is stronger for meeting and repelling an attacker.
rows.anchor: وقدمت الأيمان على الشمائل لأنها الجهة التي هي القوية في ملاقاة العدو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses grateful as affirming divine unity; he and others also gloss it as believing, since gratitude for God’s gift entails faith.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس شاكرين موحدين وعنه وعن غيره مؤمنين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses grateful as thankful for God’s blessings.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل شاكرين لنعمتك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan explains the phrase as steadfast in obedience and notes that only a few give thanks.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: ثابتين على طاعتك ولا يشكرك إلا القليل منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that most will not be grateful may be part of Iblis’s oath or an independent report; his prediction may be conjecture or knowledge.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون داخلة في خبر القسم معطوفة على جوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proposed sources for Iblis’s knowledge include seeing the Preserved Tablet, learning that few servants are grateful, revelation to angels, angelic foreknowledge, or seeing Adam’s descendants weaker than himself.
rows.anchor: إما رؤيته ذلك في اللوح المحفوظ أو استفادته من قوله وقليل من عبادي الشكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says human beings have nineteen bodily powers drawing toward physical pleasure, while a single, initially weak intellect calls toward worship of God.
rows.anchor: أو يكون قوى ابن آدم تسعة عشر قوة وهي خمس حواس ظاهرة وخمس باطنة

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: The majority take the pronoun in get out of it to refer to Paradise, as in the earlier command to descend.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على أن الضمير عائد على الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three commands successively order descent, announce humiliation, and specify expulsion with blame and rejection.
rows.anchor: وهذه ثلاث أوامر أمر بالهبوط مطلقا، وأمر بالخروج مخبرا أنه ذو صغار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses مذؤوما as cursed.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: مذؤما لعينا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses مذؤوما as blamed.
rows.anchor: ملوما، وقال مجاهد: منفيا، وقيل: ممقوتا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses مذؤوما as expelled.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: منفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses take مذؤوما as detested and مدحورا as driven away from mercy, good, Paradise, divine enabling, or the company of special believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ممقوتا ومدحورا مبعدا من رحمة الله أو من الخير أو من الجنة

rows.speaker: الزهري وأبو جعفر والأعمش
rows.claim: These readers pronounce مذوما without hamza; it may be a softened form of the hamzated root or derive from the unhamzated verb ذام.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وأبو جعفر والأعمش: مذوما بضم الذال من غير همز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مدحورا may be a second circumstantial accusative, a circumstance attached to the pronoun in مذؤما, or an adjective describing it.
rows.anchor: وانتصب مدحورا على أنه حال ثانية على من جوز ذلك

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the initial lam of لمن with fatḥa as an emphatic lam; man is relative, and the following oath clause supplies its predicate.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور لمن بفتح اللام الابتداء ومن موصولة

rows.speaker: الجحدري وعصمة عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: These transmitters read the lam in لمن with kasra, prompting several disputed syntactic explanations.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وعصمة عن أبي بكر عن عاصم لمن تبعك منهم بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya takes the kasra reading to mean I will fill Hell for those who follow you; Abu Hayyan objects that the oath lam cannot govern preceding words.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عطية: المعنى لأجل من تبعك منهم لأملأن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes the oath clause the subject and لمن تبعك its predicate, but Abu Hayyan says this conflicts with the clause’s status as a sentencelike oath response.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري بمعنى لمن تبعك منهم الوعيد وهو قوله لأملأن جهنم

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل عبد الرحمن بن أحمد بن الحسن الرازي
rows.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi links the lam to the preceding words for blame and expulsion, meaning Iblis is sent out under those descriptions because of his followers.
rows.anchor: اللام متعلقة من الذأم والدحر ومعناه اخرج بهاتين الصفتين لأجل أتباعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In منكم, the address to Iblis expands to include those who follow him, with plural masculine agreement overriding their third-person status.
rows.anchor: ومعنى منكم منك وممن تبعك فغلب الخطاب على الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command begins with an understood and We said; its explanation had already appeared in al-Baqara, where the food is called abundant, a phrase omitted here for brevity.
rows.anchor: أي وقلنا يا آدم وتقدم تفسير هذه الآية في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording in al-Baqara is fuller because that sūra is Medinan, whereas this Meccan passage expresses the same meaning more briefly.
rows.anchor: وحذف رغدا هنا على سبيل الاختصار وأثبت هناك لأن تلك مدنية وهذه مكية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Iblis’s whisper reached the pair in Paradise while he was on earth, through a power God created in him; Ibn ʿAtiyya calls this weak and says the Quran’s wording refutes it.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: وصلت وسوسته لهما في الجنة وهو في الأرض بالقوة التي خلقها الله له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other accounts place Iblis in heaven while Adam and Eve came to him, at Paradise’s gate, or entering them through the serpent’s mouth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان في السماء وكانا يخرجان إليه، وقيل: من باب الجنة وهما بها

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani says Satan inspired the couple; Ibn al-Qushayri says he presented them with embellished thoughts, but Abu Hayyan says both conflict with the apparent dialogue, conversation, and oath.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني: ألهمهما، وقال ابن القشيري: أورد عليهما الخواطر المزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading is that Satan spoke to them; the purpose clause means he aimed to expose their nakedness and lower their standing, though some take it as an outcome he did not know in advance.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن اللام لام كي قصد إبداء سوآتهما

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says exposing nakedness has always been regarded as shameful by instinct and reason, reflecting his Muʿtazili view of rational moral judgments.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن كشف العورة من عظائم الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of the couple’s private parts is the front and rear; one view says neither saw their own or each other’s before eating, while Qatada uses the shameful part for the whole body.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه يراد مدلول سوءاتهما نفسهما وهما الفرج والدبر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says their nakedness stands for their whole bodies, named by the most shameful part exposed in humans.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة كنى بسوءاتهما عن جميع بدنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers vary on the passive reading of covered, its singular or plural nakedness, and whether hamza is eased into a doubled or single wāw; plural may replace dual or describe the four private parts.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ بالجمع فهو من وضع الجمع موضع التثنية كراهة اجتماع مثلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception after what your Lord forbade you is understood as an exception from the purpose: He forbade it only from aversion to your becoming angels; supplying the noun aversion is preferable to supplying the particle no.
rows.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من المفعول من أجله أي ما نهاكما ربكما لشيء إلا كراهة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari sees evidence that angels occupy a higher rank than humans.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن الملائكة بالمنظر الأعلى

rows.speaker: ابن فورك
rows.claim: Ibn Furak says the verse does not prove angels outrank humans, since being angels may mean being free of appetite for food.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فورك: لا حجة في هذه الآية على أن الملائكة أفضل من البشر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن بن علي والضحاك ويحيى بن كثير والزهري وابن حكيم
rows.claim: These readers pronounce malakayn with kasra on the lām; the tree of immortality and imperishable kingdom elsewhere supports this sense of angelic or immortal status.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والحسن بن علي والضحاك ويحيى بن كثير والزهري وابن حكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase those who remain forever explains the intended promise as never dying and remaining in Paradise.
rows.anchor: ومن الخالدين من الذين لا يموتون ويبقون في الجنة ساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan did not rely on whispering or speech alone: he swore to convince the pair that he was sincere.
rows.anchor: لم يكتف إبليس بالوسوسة وهو الإلقاء في خفية سرا ولا بالقول حتى أقسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal form qāsama normally implies participation, but here it means he swore to them even though they did not join his oath.
rows.anchor: وأما هنا فمعنى وقاسمهما أقسم لهما لأن اليمين لم يشاركاه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line is cited as evidence for the wording of the oath with bāʾ and a two-sided form.
rows.anchor: وقاسمهما بالله جهدا لأنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form fāʿala can sometimes carry the meaning of the simple causative form afʿala.
rows.anchor: وفاعل قد يأتي بمعنى أفعل نحو باعدت الشيء وأبعدته

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya explains reciprocal qāsama as swearing to them, with their accepting and attending to the oath making the action reciprocal; Abu Hayyan notes that the oath itself is still one-sided.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية وقاسمهما أي حلف لهما وهي مفاعلة إذ قبول المحلوف له

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari imagines the pair asking Iblis whether he swears by God, or says he swore by his counsel and they accepted it, or that he exerted himself like a partner in oath-taking.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: كأنه قال لهما أقسم لكما أني لمن الناصحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has qāsamahumā bi-llāh; the attachment of لكما may be to an omitted adviser, to the adjective sincere, or to another understood expression, with differing analyses of the definite article.
rows.anchor: وقرىء وقاسمهما بالله ولكما متعلق بمحذوف تقديره ناصح لكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan drew them into eating through deception: pretending to advise while concealing fraud, tempting them with angelic status or immortality, and swearing sincerity.
rows.anchor: أي استنزلهما إلى الأكل من الشجرة بغروره أي بخداعه إياهما

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari gives two origins for the idiom: lowering a bucket with no water as a false promise, or emboldening someone to act; the second is linked to a form meaning make bold.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري: لهذه الكلمة أصلان

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: A saying says Satan deceived Adam and Adam was deceived, while those who are deceived by reliance on God are rightly drawn to Him; similar wording is attributed to Qatada and Ibn Umar.
rows.anchor: ومن كلام بعض العلماء: خدع الشيطان آدم فانخدع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن جبير
rows.claim: They say Adam and Eve had a glass-like nail covering; after eating it was stripped away, leaving a reminder on their fingers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة وابن جبير: كان عليهما ظفر كاس

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says a light had covered each person’s nakedness and vanished when they ate.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: كان عليهما نور يستر عورة كل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the lost light left a remnant as fingernails or toenails to remind them and their descendants to seek forgiveness; this is compared to the remaining white mark on Uways al-Qarani after his leprosy healed.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان عليهما نور فنقص وتجسد منه شيء في أظفار اليدين والرجلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the exposed nakedness as livelihood and distress, but Abu Hayyan says that reading conflicts with the wording and the majority.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: لم يقصد بالسوأة العورة والمعنى انكشف لهما معايشهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Eve ate first without effect, and the exposure occurred only after Adam ate.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أكلت حواء أول فلم يصبها شيء ثم آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They began joining leaves together to cover themselves after Paradise’s garments had been stripped; the pronoun most likely means their two naked parts.
rows.anchor: أي جعلا يلصقان ورقة على ورقة ويلصقانهما بعد ما كانت كساهما حلل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attached pronoun cannot straightforwardly refer to Adam and Eve because Arabic forbids this combination of a connected subject and object pronoun here, unless a noun such as bodies is omitted.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز زيد ضربه ولا ضربه زيد ولا زيد مر به زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the leaves as olive leaves.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الورق الذي خصفا منه ورق الزيتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others suggest fig or banana leaves, but neither is established by the Quran or a sound hadith.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ورق شجر التين، وقيل: ورق الموز ولم يثبت تعيينها

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads ṭafiqa with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال وطفقا بفتح الفاء

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reads yakhṣifān from the form afʿala, which may mean the basic action or causatively mean they made themselves cover.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري يخصفان من أخصف

rows.speaker: الحسن والأعرج ومجاهد وابن وثاب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce yakhṣifān with fatḥa on the first syllable and a doubled ṣād, with further reported variants in its vowel pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعرج ومجاهد وابن وثاب يخصفان بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: In a report from Mahbub, Hasan keeps the doubled ṣād but gives fatḥa to the khāʾ; this is also reported from Ibn Burayda and Yaʿqub.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن فيما روى عنه محبوب كذلك إلا أنه فتح الخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading doubles the consonant in yakhṣṣifān from the form khaṣṣafa.
rows.anchor: وقرىء يخصفان بالتشديد من خصف على وزن فعل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن يزيد
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Yazid reads with ḍamma on yāʾ and khāʾ and a doubled, kasra ṣād.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن يزيد يخصفان بضم الياء والخاء وتشديد الصاد وكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A history of Ibn Abi Khaythama records Adam being called a prophet spoken to, supporting direct speech to him.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام سئل عن آدم فقال: نبي مكلم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say the call came through revelation; they cite Moses’ unique distinction as God’s interlocutor and the intercession report, while another passage can be reconciled by limiting Moses’ distinction to earthly speech.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: إن النداء كان بواسطة الوحي ويؤيده أن موسى عليه السلام هو الذي خص من بين العالم بالكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view says the call was addressed literally to Adam alone, since no report says God spoke to Eve; a call may address someone by name, kind, or description even when unstated here.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النداء لآدم على الحقيقة ولم يرو قط أن الله كلم حواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted question is grammatically governed by an omitted saying verb and serves as reproach, drawing attention to their oversight.
rows.anchor: والجملة معمولة لقول محذوف أي قائلا: ألم أنهكما وهو استفهام معناه العتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The near demonstrative was used when the tree was accessible and eating permitted, while the distant form at reproach intimates the coming separation and expulsion.
rows.anchor: ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة إشارة لطيفة حيث كان مباحا له الأكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that God had told them of Satan’s enmity refers to the earlier warning that he must not cause their expulsion; this is the covenant Adam forgot on the literal sense of forgetting.
rows.anchor: وأقل لكما إشارة إلى قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satan’s enmity was evident because he had refused to prostrate and threatened to mislead Adam’s descendants.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس بين العداوة حيث أبى السجود وقال لأقعدن لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God asked Adam whether the abundance of other trees had not sufficed; Adam says he thought no creature would swear falsely by God, and God then sends him to earn his subsistence through labor.
rows.anchor: روي أنه تعالى قال لآدم: ألم يكن لك فيما منحتك من شجر الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report continues that Adam learned ironwork and farming, then plowed, irrigated, harvested, threshed, winnowed, kneaded, and baked.
rows.anchor: وعلم صنعة الحديد وأمر بالحرث فحرث وسقى وحصد ودرس وذر وعجن وخبز

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy says, Did you not both refrain from that tree, and were you not told?
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ألم تنهيا عن تلكما الشجرة وقيل لكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjoining plumage or adornment with clothing indicates that it is a distinct category rather than part of clothing.
rows.anchor: وعطف الريش على لباسا يقتضي المغايرة وأنه قسيم للباس لا قسم منه

rows.speaker: عثمان وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والسلمي وعلي بن الحسين وزيد وأبو رجاء وزر بن حبيش وعاصم وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers use the variant riyāshan, which receives several lexical explanations.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عثمان وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والسلمي وعلي بن الحسين وابنه زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take rīsh and riyāsh as synonymous verbal nouns meaning God bestowed favor.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هما مصدران بمعنى واحد راشه الله يريشه ريشا ورياشا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says riyāsh is a plural of rīsh.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: جمع ريش كشعب وشعاب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says both forms mean clothing.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هما اللباس

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the words cover clothes and wealth, by analogy with lubs and libās.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: هما ما يستر من ثياب ومال

rows.speaker: معبد الجهني
rows.claim: Maʿbad al-Juhani glosses riyāsh as livelihood.
rows.anchor: وقال معبد الجهني: الرياش المعاش

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says rīsh means food and drink while riyāsh means acquired wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: الريش الأكل والشرب والرياش المال المستفاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another lexical view distinguishes inner garments as rīsh and outer garments as riyāsh.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الريش ما بطن والرياش ما ظهر

rows.speaker: الصاحبان والكسائي
rows.claim: The two readers and al-Kisaʾi read libās al-taqwā in the accusative, coordinated with the preceding accusative; the rest of the seven read it in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الصاحبان والكسائي: ولباس التقوى بالنصب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the nominative as a new clause with an omitted subject, and that is better as a predicate on this analysis.
rows.anchor: فقيل هو على إضمار مبتدأ محذوف أي وهو لباس التقوى قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows لباس to be the subject with an omitted predicate meaning it covers your nakedness, a proposal Abu Hayyan dismisses.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء أن يكون ولباس مبتدأ وخبره محذوف تقديره ولباس التقوى ساتر عوارتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent construction makes لباس التقوى a second subject, خير its predicate, and ذلك the link returning the predicate clause to the first subject.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه مبتدأ ثان وخير خبره والجملة خبر عن ولباس التقوى

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi rejects ذلك as an adjective because a demonstrative is more definite than a noun with the article; he treats it as a separator, which Abu Hayyan says is the strongest common analysis.
rows.anchor: وما ذكره الحوفي هو الصواب على أشهر الأقوال في ترتيب المعارف

rows.speaker: عبد الله وأبي
rows.claim: A reading omits ذلك, leaving a direct subject-predicate clause: the garment of piety is good.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبي ولباس التقوى خير بإسقاط ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the garment of piety literally as clothing that covers nakedness, though Abu Hayyan notes that this repeats the earlier description.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن زيد هو ستر العورة وهذا فيه تكرار

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali identifies the garment as armor, helmet, and protective bracers worn in war.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن علي: الدرع والمغفر والساعدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other literal interpretations include wool and coarse clothing, clothing against heat and cold, or the garments of the pious in the afterlife; another takes the phrase metaphorically.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الصوف ولبس الخشن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry uses al-aʿrāf for a high place, as in comparisons to a mountain crest and upright lances; horse and rooster crests take the same name because they rise above the body.
rows.anchor: ومنه عرف الفرس وعرف الديك لعلوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word six comes from an older form sidsa, with consonant substitutions and assimilation; its diminutive preserves the older sīn.
rows.anchor: الستة رتبة من العدد معروفة وأصلها سدسة

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth glosses exhorting as hastening someone; its agent is described as eager or urged on.
rows.anchor: الحث الإعجال حثثت فلانا فأحثثت قاله الليث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the command for justice as the declaration that there is no god but God, since all good begins from it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس القسط هنا لا إله إلا الله لأن أسباب الخير كلها تنشأ عنها

rows.speaker: عطاء والسدي
rows.claim: Ata and al-Suddi take justice as fairness, or as speech that is visibly good and correct.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء والسدي: العدل وما يظهر في القول كونه حسنا صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses of justice are truth and what is right.
rows.anchor: وقيل الصدق والحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, establish your faces can coordinate with the verbal noun justice by supplying that you establish; command verbs can be governed by the particle that, unlike a merely nominal maṣdar particle or a source-like kay.
rows.anchor: وأقيموا معطوف على ما ينحل إليه المصدر الذي هو القسط

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead supplies and say before the imperative, either making it dependent on that verb or joining it to the first command say.
rows.anchor: جعل الزمخشري وأقيموا على تقدير وقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical proposal joins the command to an omitted imperative such as turn toward God, then establish your faces.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وأقيموا معطوف على أمر محذوف تقديره فأقبلوا وأقيموا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: They say that when prayer comes, people should pray in every mosque rather than insist on their own mosque.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك واختاره ابن قتيبة: المعنى إذا حضرت الصلاة فصلوا في كل مسجد

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: They interpret the command as facing the Kaʿba in prayer wherever one is.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد: معناه توجهوا حيث كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says to make prostration sincere to God alone.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع: اجعلوا سجودكم خالصا لله دون غيره

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says to go to a mosque at each prayer time, making the verse an instruction to pray in congregation.
rows.anchor: أمرا بالجماعة ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: التبريزي
rows.claim: Al-Tabrizi says that if a mosque is nearby, people should establish congregational prayer there rather than go elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ذكره التبريزي

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: A further explanation from al-Rabiʿ is to bring intention to God in every prayer and direct oneself toward Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو أمر بإحضار النية لله في كل صلاة والقصد نحوه كما تقول وجهت وجهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation permits prayer anywhere on earth, since every place is a mosque where one must worship God.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه إباحة الصلاة في كل موضع من الأرض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains establish your faces as directing worship uprightly toward God at every prayer time and every place of prostration.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أي اقصدوا عبادته مستقيمين إليه غير عادلين إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to call on God may mean literal supplication, worship, or saying there is no god but God; supplication requires exclusive devotion to be answered.
rows.anchor: قيل: الدعاء على بابه أمر به مقرونا بالإخلاص

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They explain returning as resurrection: just as God originated people, He recreates them after death to reward their deeds.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة هو إعلام بالبعث

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives only the resurrection interpretation, arguing that initial creation answers denial of return and calls for sincere worship.
rows.anchor: قال: كما أنشأكم ابتداء يعيدكم احتج عليهم في إنكارهم الإعادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj likewise argues that raising people is no harder than first creating them and answers their denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهذا احتجاج عليهم في إنكارهم البعث انتهى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو العالية ومحمد بن كعب وابن جبير والسدي ومجاهد والفراء
rows.claim: A second interpretation says people return in the camps of belief and happiness or unbelief and misery already decreed for them; a similar meaning is reported from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو العالية ومحمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy’s reading says you return as two groups, one guided and one condemned to error, supporting the two-camps interpretation and making the second group a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: قراءة أبي تعودون فريقين فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses one group as the object of guided and the other as the object of an implied misled, or takes both clauses as circumstances with an omitted qad.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون فريقا مفعول هدى وفريقا مفعول أضل مضمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings say people return unsupported, return from dust to dust, or rise naked as they were created; the first echoes the Quran’s description of arriving alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى تعودون لا ناصر لكم ولا معين لقوله ولقد جئتمونا فرادى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says people are returned to dust just as they began from dust.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: كما بدأكم من التراب يعيدكم إلى التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says people are created unclothed and resurrected unclothed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه كما خلقكم عراة تبعثون عراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about error being established may mean God decreed error for them or that the punishment for error became due.
rows.anchor: ومعنى حق عليهم الضلالة أي حق عليهم من الله أو حق عليهم عقوبة الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though God is the guide and creates misguidance, the wording does not attribute misguidance to Him because the passage addresses Satan’s misleading and God’s command to justice and prayer.
rows.anchor: وجاء إسناد الهدى إلى الله ولم يجىء مقابله وفريقا أضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straying group takes devils as helpers and allies, while devils assist their disbelief and people follow their whispers; another interpretation makes the devils their religious leaders.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد حقيقة الشياطين فهم يعينونهم على كفرهم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says the verse refutes the claim that God punishes no sin or false belief unless its perpetrator consciously knows the right answer, because the strayers merely suppose they are guided.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: وهذه الآية دليل على خطأ قول من زعم أن الله تعالى لا يعذب أحدا

rows.speaker: العباس بن الفضل وسهل بن شعيب وعيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: These readers open the hamza in innahum; the wording then gives a causal explanation for error becoming due, while kasra can also carry a causal sense.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العباس بن الفضل وسهل بن شعيب وعيسى بن عمر إنهم اتخذوا بفتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says they followed Satan by obeying his commands, proving on his view that God’s knowledge did not cause their error and that they chose Satan freely.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أي تولوهم بالطاعة فيما أمروهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says pre-Islamic Arabs circled the Kaʿba naked and abstained from fatty food during pilgrimage, restricting themselves to meager provisions out of exaggerated reverence.
rows.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية يطوفون بالبيت عراة وكانوا لا يأكلون في أيام حجهم دسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says some left their clothes behind the mosque for circumambulation, stripping them if worn because they thought they could not worship in clothes stained by sin; some undressed to symbolize shedding sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان أحدهم يطوف عريانا ويدع ثيابه وراء المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adornment is what people beautify themselves with, including clothing; the commanded adornment is glossed in several ways as covering nakedness for prayer or circumambulation.
rows.anchor: والزينة فعلة من التزين وهو اسم ما يتجمل به من ثياب وغيرها

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي والزجاج
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, and al-Zajjaj identify the adornment as whatever covers the private parts during prayer.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد والسدي والزجاج

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus says a wrap or cloak is the adornment meant.
rows.anchor: وقال طاوس الشملة من الزينة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also says any covering of nakedness, even an abaya, counts as adornment.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ما وارى عورتك ولو عباءة فهو زينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the required clothing as what covers nakedness during circumambulation.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما يستر العورة في الطواف

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: A report in Muslim says Arabs circumambulated naked except the Hums, Quraysh, who supplied clothes, with men clothing men and women clothing women.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن عروة أن العرب كانت تطوف عراة إلا الخمس وهم قريش
